sentences.text:
Parveen Bee vs Shubham Saini on 4 December, 2025
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Ind:35504
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

At Indore
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Pavan Kumar Dwivedi
 On The 4 th Of December, 2025
 Misc. Appeal No. 6931 of 2024
 Parveen Bee And Others
 Versus
Shubham Saini And Others
Appearance:

Shri Satish Jain, learned counsel for the appellant
 Shri Pankaj Kumar Jain, learned counsel for the res
 Order

The appellants have filed this appeal being aggrieved by the award dated 13.08.2024 passed in claim case No.24/2022 whereby the claim petition filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act has been rejected.

2. The short facts of the case are that on 26.08.2022, the deceased Shahjad Hussain, who was working as forest guard, was going by his motorcycle to his home at village-Jaat, when he reached near Barekhan Gau- Shaala at Neemuch-Ratangarh Road, respondent No.1 came driving car number MP09-CM-6373 in a rash and negligence manner and dashed into the motorcycle of Shahjad Hussain from behind because of which he sustained grievous injuries and died during treatment at Government Hospital,
Ratangarh.

An F.I.R. was registered at crime No.113/2022 under Section 304A of IPC on 31.08.2022 for the accident occurred on NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:35504 2 MA-6931-2024 26.08.2022.
3.
The appellants filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the death of Shahjad Hussain.
The claims tribunal after recording evidence concluded in para Nos.6 to 18 that involvement of the insured vehicle was not found proved in the accident as such the claim petition was rejected.

The material which weighed with the claims tribunal for rejecting the claim petition was the absence of mentioning the vehicle number in Merg intimation which was sent on the same date i.e. on the date of accident, (Ex.P-5) by Primary Health Center, Ratangarh to police station, Ratangarh in which although accident was mentioned but reference to the vehicle was not there.

Out of the two eye witnesses, who were claimed to be there at Parveen Bee vs Shubham Saini on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116674465/
1

the time of accident i.e. Mohammad Yunush and Abdul Kaadir, one of them i.e. Mohammad Yunush was examined before the claims tribunal as AW-3, however, he denied the fact that he has seen the accident.
He stated that he came to know about the accident during the funeral procession of the deceased.
Considering this, the claims tribunal rejected the claim petition by holding that the involvement of the vehicle was not found proved.
4. However, there is a significant aspect of the matter.
There was one more eye witness who was stated to be present when the accident occurred namely Abdul Kaadir.
This person was also listed witness in police case.

The claimants had filed an application before the claims tribunal for summoning the said eye witness for his deposition before the claims tribunal, however, the same was dismissed by the claims tribunal vide order dated 02.08.2024 NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:35504 3 MA-6931-2024 by observing that it is very late in the day to summon the said witness at the fag end of trial.

5. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that this rejection of the application goes to the root of the matter in as much as it was only preponderance of probability which was required to be established by the claimants for demonstrating involvement of the insured vehicle but, due to denial of opportunity the claimants were not able to do the same.
Thus, he prays for allowing this appeal and remanding the matter back for giving opportunity to establish the involvement of the vehicle.

6. Opposing the prayer, learned counsel for the insurance company submits that there was full opportunity before the claimants to lead the evidence, however, they waited till the fag end of the trial, hence, this prayer should not be entertained.
He further submits that there is clear denial of eye witness PW-3 Mohammad Yunush that he has seen the accident.
It is thus clear that the claimants have tried to implant the witness who was not present on the spot when the accident occurred.
Looking to this conduct of the appellants, they do not deserve any chance for leading evidence of another so called eye witness.

7. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
8.

From perusal of the Challan of the criminal case it is seen that the police has listed two eye witnesses, one of them was Mohammad Yunush, who had appeared before the tribunal and other was Abdul Kaadir.

From the cross-examination of Mohammad Yunush, it is seen that he appeared to be totally lost in the maze of the proceedings before the claims tribunal, hence, NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:35504 4 MA-6931-2024 he has given incoherent answers to the questions put to him.

Considering this and the fact that the claimants have requested for examining the other eye witness Abdul Kaadir, which was denied, this Court is of the considered view that proper opportunity for proving the factum of accident by the insured vehicle has been denied to the appellants/claimants.
As such, the appeal is allowed.
The matter is remanded back to the claims tribunal so as to provide opportunity to the claimants to lead evidence of Abdul Kaadir for proving the factum of accident.
9. As such, the parties are directed to appear before the claims tribunal on 10.02.2026 and on such other dates as may be fixed by the claims tribunal in this behalf.

It is needless to say that all the Parveen Bee vs Shubham Saini on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116674465/
2 parties are free to lead the evidence in rebuttal.
(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE N.R.
